texts.preamble: Sanjay Kumar Puwar @ Sanjay Puwar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 25 November, 2022 Author: Raj Beer Singh Bench: Raj Beer Singh High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 73 Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 7974 of 2021 Applicant :- Sanjay Kumar Puwar @ Sanjay Puwar
texts.facts: The present application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Complaint Case No. 683 of 2020, under Sections 26(1), 26(2)(v)(i)(iii), 31(1) read with Section 3(1)(zz)(v)(ix) and Section 58, 59(iii) and Section 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, Police Station Kotwali Rath, District Hamirpur with the prayer that in the event of arrest, applicant may be released on bail. that as per version of complainant, the said samples were taken from one Sanjay Gupta but no person of such name is working at the shop of applicant. Referring to the facts of the matter, it was submitted that the samples have not been taken in accordance with law and rules.
texts.arguments: It has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has an apprehension that he may be arrested in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against him. Learned counsel submitted that applicant has been summoned in a complaint case. According to prosecution version, on 18.09.2018 some sample of pulse were taken from the shop of applicant, which after examination was found of sub-standard. Learned counsel submitted Sanjay Kumar Puwar @ Sanjay Puwar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 25 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79418310/ 1 It was further submitted that alleged incident has been shown of 18.09.2018 and the complaint was filed on 27.06.2020 and that the complaint is barred by period of limitation prescribed under Food Safety and Standards Act. Applicant has no criminal antecedents. It has been stated that in case, applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate during trial and would obey all conditions of bail. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the application for anticipatory bail. It may be stated that in case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.
